feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader: the experience is relevant, progressive, and supported by concrete platforms, scope, and outcomes. It reads clearly overall, but it is slightly repetitive and overpacked with overlapping sections, which dilutes impact.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior positioning: the headline, summary, and career progression at NACo strongly support leadership in digital platforms, governance, and communications systems.  
- Good credibility signals: named tools, scale metrics (10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers), and recent project examples make the profile believable and substantive.  
- Strong breadth with practical depth: combines strategy, CMS/platform work, analytics, multimedia, and AI/search in a way that feels current and marketable.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidating these would improve structure and make key strengths stand out faster.  
- Add sharper outcomes in several bullets: some points describe responsibilities more than results. Where possible, quantify gains in efficiency, engagement, adoption, or campaign performance.  
- Minor style/consistency issues: “Coleman DAVIS” is inconsistent title casing; punctuation around lists is uneven; “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; “A2/Learning” reads awkwardly; “Ranked among the top public universities…” is low-value filler. No major misspellings found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and public-sector focus, but it overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience. It would be stronger with one sharper value proposition and a few concrete signals of scope.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten and reduce list-like phrasing; replace “platforms, governance models and content operations” with a more direct summary of outcomes and scope.
- Add one concrete scale marker from recent experience, e.g. “10,000+ page Drupal migration” or “3.5M annual page views,” to increase impact.
- Recast the second sentence to emphasize leadership outcomes: modernization, governance, analytics, and audience experience.
- Suggested rewrite: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing public-sector communications through enterprise web platforms, digital governance, and content operations. Led large-scale Drupal and analytics transformations for high-volume, mission-driven organizations, including a 10,000+ page website serving 3.5M annual views, while advancing editorial systems, multimedia programs, and AI-enabled search experiences.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with core competencies and recent projects; consider narrowing to “AI-enabled search experiences.”
- “Enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production” repeats multiple skills sections almost verbatim.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. It would be sharper if phrased more distinctly and weighted toward senior, recent strengths.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten and standardize phrasing for parallel structure; e.g. use all noun phrases: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, dashboards and reporting systems • Multi-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integrations • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations
- Consider replacing “Enterprise website modernization” with “Enterprise web modernization” for cleaner wording.
- “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” could be more concrete as “Analytics, dashboards and reporting systems.”
- “AI-enabled search and content experiences” is strong, but “content discovery” is slightly clearer and less vague.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section substantially repeats the header summary and Topline Skills; consider making Core Competencies more concise or more executive-level.
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” also overlaps with the dedicated Multimedia/Technical sections.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads like an expanded repeat of the recent roles rather than a distinct footer highlight. Tightening phrasing and making the format more uniform will improve scanability and impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements
- Add a one-line intro such as “Selected recent projects” and keep all entries in parallel verb-led format.
- Tighten wording: “hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search, and bill-level AI chat” is strong; cut filler like “designed for continued campaign growth.”
- Standardize style and punctuation: use serial commas, consistent capitalization, and spell out “10 x 20-foot” instead of “10×20-foot” for CV consistency.
- Emphasize outcomes or scope where possible, even briefly, e.g., audience, campaign purpose, or organizational use.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series closely repeat achievements already covered in the current freelance and NACo roles.
- The anniversary campaign may add the most unique value because it introduces archival media and conference display work not emphasized elsewhere.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: colemandavis4@gmail.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a broad responsibility list and overlaps heavily with the header, skills, and “Recent Projects.” Tighten it around 3–5 high-impact outcomes and name the most distinctive work.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + client type + value: “Embedded as a full-time freelance consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvements across Drupal, content operations, governance, and campaign delivery.”
- Replace generic verbs (“support,” “advise,” “deliver”) with ownership verbs: led, built, launched, redesigned, standardized, improved.
- Consolidate into fewer bullets focused on distinct outcomes:
- Built Drupal campaign/microsite experiences with modular content, custom navigation, and downloadable member toolkits.
- Improved enterprise web operations by standardizing workflows, analytics, and cross-team publishing processes.
- Led AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval design, structured content workflows, and user discovery experience.
- Provided front-end/CMS implementation and troubleshooting for high-traffic public-facing properties.
- Add metrics if available: number of sites/pages, users, publishers, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, search accuracy, or workflow time saved.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search” and microsite work already appear in Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level and outcome-focused.
- Governance/analytics/platform modernization also overlap with the NACo role; emphasize what is new in this engagement.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize the biggest outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management details already covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, leading web modernization, analytics, governance, budget, and multi-channel operations across web, email, social, and video.”
- Combine the strongest achievements into outcome-led bullets: “Led redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make impact more explicit where possible: add team size, budget, production volume, engagement growth, reporting speed, or efficiency gains for analytics/governance/studio buildout.
- Tighten softer bullets: replace “Strengthened digital operations…” with specifics such as governance model launched, standards adopted, or planning system implemented.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this version focused on enterprise leadership and scale.
- Video-program language overlaps with earlier NACo entries and Recent Projects; emphasize building the in-house studio, not recurring content production.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more specific to what you personally owned at this level: channel operations, editorial coordination, and the launch/growth of recurring advocacy video.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to focus on scope and ownership: “Managed day-to-day digital communications operations across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, improving editorial coordination and advocacy publishing.”
- Tighten bullets and lead with actions: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more outcome-oriented: “Launched and produced a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one sharper line: “Built stronger cross-team editorial planning and more consistent digital publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Helping scale” and “helped improve” sound soft; use direct ownership.
- Avoid repeating governance/workflow language already used in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and work experience. It should be tightened to emphasize senior leadership scope and distinctive value rather than repeating generic communications terms.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less repetitive phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial governance and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy communications
- Audience strategy and content planning
- Consider swapping “messaging” for “communications” to sound more senior and operationally aligned with the CV.
- If space allows, make one line outcome-oriented, e.g. “Enterprise digital strategy for high-volume public-sector platforms.”
- Keep this section at capability level; save platform, analytics, and AI specifics for the other Topline Skills sections.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” already echo the header and Core Competencies.
- “Audience-focused content planning” is close to experience bullets on editorial coordination and storytelling; avoid expanding it further here.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it overlaps heavily with Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize current, differentiating strengths tied to recent Drupal modernization and AI/search work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a raw tool list to a sharper capability stack: “Drupal & CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations • Workflow automation • Airtable systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Drop lower-signal or older/platform-specific items unless central to target roles: remove “jQuery” and consider removing “WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages” from this topline section.
- Put the strongest recent themes first: Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, API/workflow integration.
- If space allows, use one outcome-oriented phrase: “Drupal modernization for high-volume public-sector sites” or “AI-enabled search for complex policy content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “CMS modernization,” “workflow automation,” and “AI-enabled search experiences” already appear in Core Competencies.
- Platform/tool lists are already covered in Technical + IT; avoid repeating the same inventory here.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value analytical leadership and decision support, not just platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool list to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Analytics strategy & reporting • GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework design • Executive/leadership dashboards • SEO, UX and performance analysis”
- Put the most strategic items first: KPI design, executive reporting, analytics strategy, then tools.
- Tighten wording: change “Leadership reporting” to “Executive dashboarding” or “Executive reporting.”
- If accurate, add one stronger outcome-oriented phrase such as “decision-ready reporting” or “insight-driven optimization” to signal impact.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Technical + IT > Data, Analytics & Optimization”; keep Topline Skills more strategic and leave full tool coverage to Technical + IT.
- Avoid repeating every platform here if they already appear in recent NACo experience bullets.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong supporting skill area, but it reads generic and overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies and several NACo bullets. Make it more senior, operational, and distinctive.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Multimedia Production, Studio & Event Operations**
- Replace with tighter, higher-level bullets such as:
- Broadcast-quality video production and post-production
- Livestream and hybrid event production
- PTZ camera and in-house studio operations
- Virtual event technical delivery and show flow coordination
- If accurate, strengthen one bullet with scope: “Livestream and hybrid event production for advocacy, member and conference programming”
- Keep tool-level detail like editing software out of this section since it already appears under “Technical + IT”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestreaming” and “Hybrid and virtual event production” partially duplicate Core Competencies’ “Multimedia production and livestream operations”
- “Studio operations” also echoes the NACo role bullet about building the in-house video studio

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Since recent experience is strongly Drupal-led, this item should either sharpen platform depth or be consolidated.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: “Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages” is fine, but consider “Drupal (enterprise/public-sector) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages.”
- Add light proficiency/context instead of a raw list, e.g. “Enterprise CMS platforms: Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages; lightweight publishing with GitHub Pages.”
- If space allows, signal scale where supported by experience: “Drupal (10,000+ page migration; microsites; multi-publisher governance).”
- Keep wording platform-focused here and leave development terms to the separate coding section.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is nearly duplicated by Topline Skills > “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Consider removing one section or differentiating this one as “CMS Platforms” and the other as broader technical capabilities.
- “GitHub Pages” may feel minor versus enterprise platforms unless supported elsewhere.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools that support recent Drupal, analytics, automation, and AI/search work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename/refocus to: “Front-End & Technical Implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery, API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions”
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless used consistently elsewhere; “HTML, CSS, JavaScript” is cleaner.
- If space allows, add specificity tied to recent work: “API integrations, tag deployment, edge scripting, CI/CD automation” instead of only tool names.
- Best upgrade: connect tools to outcomes in recent roles rather than listing here alone, e.g., GTM/Workers/GitHub Actions in project or experience bullets.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- “Workflow automation” in Topline Skills may also overlap with GitHub Actions unless this section stays narrowly technical.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems capability. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools” to better match the tools listed.
- Group by function for clarity and concision: “Automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Project/work management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | Collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams.”
- If space allows, add light context tied to recent work: “used to build editorial planning, approvals, cross-team coordination, and lightweight automation workflows.”
- If you have proof points, replace 1–2 tool names with outcomes in experience bullets instead, e.g., automated reporting, reduced manual steps, or improved publishing coordination.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same phrasing elsewhere.
- Slack/Teams are very common; keep only if collaboration platforms are genuinely important to target roles.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Clear and relevant, but it reads as a vendor list rather than a capability signal. Since email leadership already appears strongly in recent roles, this item should stay concise and emphasize platform breadth without repeating newsletter management.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms
- Tighten the line to: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights & Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
- If accurate, add one qualifier for scope/value, e.g. “enterprise email automation,” “member communications,” or “campaign journeys” rather than just tool names.
- Keep platform names standardized and current; “Customer Insights & Journeys” is cleaner than using a slash.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid adding claims about newsletters, audience size, or email strategy here; those are already covered in the NACo experience entries.
- If Dynamics 365 was only lightly used, consider dropping it to avoid overstating depth versus stronger platforms.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it largely duplicates the “Analytics, Insights & Optimization” topline skills section and reads as a generic keyword dump. This item should be tighter, more technical, and avoid repeating broader capability language already covered elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad terms with more specific tools/methods: “GA4 • Google Tag Manager • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Microsoft Clarity • SEO analysis • Experimentation”
- Drop “Dashboarding,” since reporting/dashboard capability is already implied by Looker Studio and Power BI.
- Consider renaming the heading to “Analytics & Experimentation Tools” to make the list feel more concrete and less repetitive.
- If space allows elsewhere, tie this stack to impact in recent roles rather than here; keep this section tool-focused only.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially overlaps with Topline Skills [3] (“Analytics, Insights & Optimization”); avoid repeating the same exact sequence.
- “SEO” and “A/B testing” are capabilities, not platforms; they may fit better in competencies than in Technical + IT.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with the stronger 2018–2024 NACo entries. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with clearer scope and any available metrics.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize early-stage team building and hands-on production: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team, improving execution across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add concrete outputs if possible: website size/traffic at the time, number of livestreams or weekly videos produced, audience growth, email volume, or turnaround improvements.
- Tighten the second sentence: “Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate.”
- If accurate, add one measurable operational result: faster publishing, more consistent content cadence, increased engagement, or expanded in-house production capacity.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this entry focused on launching/building the function rather than scaling it.
- “strengthening workflows” is repeated elsewhere; use a more specific contribution here.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch, but it reads generic and overlaps with later multimedia/digital roles. Emphasize the distinctive “firsts,” cross-functional coordination, and any scale or outputs.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the standout achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities; launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination, and production.”
- Tighten “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials” into a clearer outcome-focused phrase, e.g., “Produced digital and multimedia content to support program communications and policy storytelling.”
- If possible, add scope: number of projects supported, podcast episodes launched, internal stakeholders served, or audiences reached.
- Consider a two-part structure: research/program support first, then podcast/multimedia leadership second.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid broadly repeating “digital content production” and “multimedia” language already covered more strongly in 2015–2024 roles.
- Don’t overstate team leadership here; later roles already establish progression into digital leadership.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid supporting skills list, but it mixes software with capabilities and repeats multimedia themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize tools only, with the strongest, most current production capabilities implied elsewhere.
